title: Episode 262: 🇳🇱 Chaos with Sean Parent! Bikes, Buses, Waffles & More!

sentences.en: I put together specifically, I got invited to give a keynote at Pacific C++, and it happened to coincide with the 30th anniversary of generic programming.
sentences.zh: 我特别准备了一场演讲，我应邀在太平洋 C++ 大会上做主旨演讲，这正好赶上泛型编程诞生 30 周年。

sentences.en: So it was 30 years after Alex Stepanoff and Dave Musser coined the term generic programming.
sentences.zh: 所以那是阿历克斯·斯捷潘诺夫和大卫·穆瑟创造“泛型编程”这个术语的 30 年后。

sentences.en: And I thought it really deserved a proper covering of kind of the history of generic programming and where it came from and why it's a thing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得确实应该好好回顾一下泛型编程的历史、它的起源以及它为什么重要。

sentences.en: And so I put together that talk, and I'm pretty proud of the talk because I ran it past Alex before I gave it, and Alex's comment was that he couldn't do it better himself.
sentences.zh: 于是我准备了那场演讲，我对它挺自豪的，因为我在演讲前先给阿历克斯看过了，他的评价是他自己也做不出比这更好的了。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 262, recorded on October 10th, 2025.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看 ADSP 播客第 262 期，录制于 2025 年 10 月 10 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we primarily interview Sean Parent at C++ Under the Sea, but this episode is pure chaos.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天我和共同主持布莱斯主要在 C++ Under the Sea 大会上采访了肖恩·帕伦特，但这一期纯属一片混乱。

sentences.en: We talk about generic programming, but also bikes, buses, waffles, and more.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了泛型编程，还有自行车、公交车、华夫饼等等。

sentences.en: And with that, we will transition to not Sean Parrott, but Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将把话筒交给肖恩……不是帕罗特，是肖恩·帕伦特。

sentences.en: Apparently we're getting t-shirts made, according to Bryce.
sentences.zh: 根据布莱斯的说法，显然我们要定制 T 恤了。

sentences.en: The idea is the t-shirt would have the parrot, but with like, you know, a cartoonized version of Sean's face on it.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是 T 恤上会有那只鹦鹉，但带有肖恩面部的卡通化版本。

sentences.en: How do we feel about that, Sean?
sentences.zh: 肖恩，我们对此有什么感想？

sentences.en: There's a bobblehead of me from CBPCon, so...
sentences.zh: 我在 CBPCon 上有一个摇头娃娃，所以……
等等，你有一个摇头娃娃？

sentences.en: You have a Sean Parent bobblehead?
sentences.zh: 你有一个肖恩·帕伦特的摇头娃娃？

sentences.en: I could maybe try to find it for your wedding buddy.
sentences.zh: 我或许可以试着为你的婚礼找一个，老兄。

sentences.en: That's a pretty good wedding gift, folks.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是个相当不错的结婚礼物，各位。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like a limited edition item, so there's probably a fixed number in the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来像是个限量版商品，所以世界上可能只有固定数量。

sentences.en: I mean, we recorded a couple months ago.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们是几个月前录的。

sentences.en: Or do we have to start leaving?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们得开始离开了？

sentences.en: Wait, when they kick us out?
sentences.zh: 等等，他们什么时候把我们赶出去？

sentences.en: You're leaving to the train soon.
sentences.zh: 你很快就要去赶火车了。

sentences.en: Are you going straight from here, or...?
sentences.zh: 你是直接从这儿过去，还是……？

sentences.en: We can go to the hotel.
We can go to the hotel.
So, wait, actually, do we have to leave right now?
sentences.zh: 所以，等等，其实我们现在就得离开吗？

sentences.en: Should we pause this and then resume at the hotel, or do we have, like, ten minutes?
sentences.zh: 我们应该暂停一下，然后到酒店再继续，还是说我们还有大约十分钟？

sentences.en: Are we being told to leave right now?
sentences.zh: 我们现在就被告知要离开了吗？
我们去了解更多信息吧。

sentences.en: I think we should pause for now and get more information.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们现在应该暂停并了解更多信息。

sentences.en: We were here with Sean at the venue.
sentences.zh: 我们和肖恩在会场这里。

sentences.en: We talked to a bunch of folks, everyone but Sean, even though that's how we started this off.
sentences.zh: 我们和大家聊了一群人，除了肖恩以外的每个人，尽管我们一开始就是这么开场的。

sentences.en: We said, we're about to talk to Sean, and then we talked to, like, six different people, and you got collected by a couple different people.
sentences.zh: 我们说，我们马上要和肖恩聊聊，然后我们和大约六个不同的人聊了，而你被几波不同的人给叫走了。

sentences.en: I have no idea, but we should get out.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道，但我们得撤了。

sentences.en: We can also record outside at the bus station.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以在公交车站外面录音。

sentences.en: We've never recorded at a bus station.
sentences.zh: 我们还从来没在公交车站录过音。

sentences.en: Yeah, you want to see something?
So, Bryce, this morning, he sent out on the Slack channel, like, he doesn't know whether he can find his way to the venue, because he couldn't get a cab within an hour.
sentences.zh: 所以，布莱斯今天早上在 Slack 频道里发消息说，他不知道自己能不能找到去会场的路，因为他在一个小时内根本叫不到出租车。

sentences.en: But we're in a European city, right?
sentences.zh: 但我们是在一个欧洲城市，对吧？

sentences.en: We have buses running every 15 minutes, and they're on time, and they're on Google Maps.
sentences.zh: 我们的公交车每 15 分钟一班，而且准时，还能在谷歌地图上查到。

sentences.en: So, like, everybody just wondered, like, why can't Bryce just take the bus, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，大家当时都在纳闷，为什么布莱斯就不能坐公交车呢，对吧？

sentences.en: Listen, folks, I would love to side with you, but I was also in the position of not being able to find an Uber.
sentences.zh: 听着，各位，我很想站在你们那边，但我也曾陷入叫不到 Uber 的处境。

sentences.en: I looked in the public transit.
It said it was going to be 30 minutes, and at that point, I had wasted 15 minutes ordering
sentences.zh: 它说需要 30 分钟，而那时我已经浪费了 15 分钟来叫车

sentences.en: and canceling three different Ubers, and I had already waited five minutes into a 19-minute wait for an Uber.
sentences.zh: 并且取消了三个不同的 Uber，而且在等待 Uber 的 19 分钟里我已经等了五分钟。

sentences.en: We discovered today that a lot of the trains ended up being canceled, and that's why Ubers...
sentences.zh: 我们今天发现，很多火车最终都被取消了，这就是为什么 Uber 会……

sentences.en: Because last year, I Ubered a couple times to and from.
sentences.zh: 因为去年我曾坐 Uber 往返过几次。
我们从来没遇到过这个问题。

sentences.en: I did look into public transit, and I had to walk, like, five minutes.
sentences.zh: 我确实查过公共交通，我得步行大约五分钟。

sentences.en: The whole thing was going to take 27 minutes.
sentences.zh: 整趟行程要花 27 分钟。

sentences.en: I've had mine for six years now, and it's as good as new.
sentences.zh: 我的已经用了六年了，依然跟新的一样。

sentences.en: Bryce and I had the same problem today, that we were trying to get here, and honestly, I think the solution is either the hotel or the conference should just have, like, rentable
sentences.zh: 布莱斯和我今天遇到了同样的问题，我们试图来到这里，老实说，我觉得解决办法要么是酒店或会议主办方应该直接提供那种租赁的

sentences.en: bikes for, like, 10 euros a day or something, because that's when we were in Aarhus in Denmark.
sentences.zh: 自行车，比如一天 10 欧元左右，因为我们在丹麦奥胡斯时就是这样的。

sentences.en: This is the Netherlands way, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是荷兰的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like, you just ride a bike.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你直接骑辆自行车就行。

sentences.en: I mean, the problem is that all the locals don't have one bike.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，问题在于当地人并不是只有一辆自行车。

sentences.en: I've heard that it's per capita.
There's more bikes than there are people.
sentences.zh: 自行车的数量比人口还要多。

sentences.en: And so there is no need for a more elaborate infrastructure, which I actually love.
sentences.zh: 因此根本不需要更复杂的设施，我其实很喜欢这样。

sentences.en: I love that, you know, Netherlands and Europe in general, it's more eco-friendly, it's better for your health, yada, yada, yada.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢荷兰以及整个欧洲更加环保，对健康更有益，等等等等。

sentences.en: So I wasn't actually upset at Uber.
sentences.zh: 所以我其实并不是生 Uber 的气。

sentences.en: I just wanted to get there faster, but I looked into it, and, like, there is not the widely availability-ness of, like, limes or birds.
sentences.zh: 我只是想更快到达那里，但我查过了，并没有那种随处可租的 Lime 或 Bird。

sentences.en: Like, they have scooters and bikes.
sentences.zh: 就像他们有滑板车和自行车一样。

sentences.en: Like, when we were in Copenhagen, a couple times we just hopped on a lime bike, which, like, you can just whip out your phone, you scan a QR code, and you're off to the races.
sentences.zh: 比如我们在哥本哈根时，有好几次我们直接骑上了一辆 Lime 自行车，你只需要掏出手机，扫个二维码，就可以出发了。

sentences.en: I think in the Netherlands, they're less available because everyone just has so many bikes, personally.
sentences.zh: 我个人觉得在荷兰它们没那么常见，是因为每个人都有太多自行车了。

sentences.en: So if you're not from here, you kind of just are screwed a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不是本地人，你基本上就有点惨了。

sentences.en: But you're not screwed because Uber typically is not that bad.
sentences.zh: 但你也不算太惨，因为 Uber 通常没那么糟糕。

sentences.en: It just happened to be that the trains weren't working today.
sentences.zh: 只是今天刚好火车瘫痪了。

sentences.en: And I heard, actually, from Andrew, one of the co-organizers of the conference, that someone, I don't know how far away they were, but they were going to train in.
sentences.zh: 而且我从大会的联合组织者之一安德鲁那里听说，有人——我不知道他们离得多远——原本打算坐火车来。

sentences.en: And then the train was broken, so they just cycled in.
sentences.zh: 结果火车坏了，于是他们直接骑自行车过来了。

sentences.en: And I asked how far, and the answer was, he was only 30 minutes late.
sentences.zh: 我问有多远，得到的回答是，他只迟到了 30 分钟。

sentences.en: I mean, Andrew's right actually there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，安德鲁说的其实没错。

sentences.en: We could get the full distance.
sentences.zh: 我们本来可以骑完整段距离的。

sentences.en: But I am imagining that this person, like, hopped on, like, a serious road bike and did, like, a decent workout on the way here.
sentences.zh: 但我猜这个人肯定是骑上了一辆专业的公路自行车，在来这里的路上进行了相当强度的锻炼。

sentences.en: But, unfortunately, there is not the availability of these bikes for foreigners.
sentences.zh: 但遗憾的是，并没有为外国人提供这种便利的自行车。

sentences.en: We should have bought our own bikes.
sentences.zh: 我们本该买自己的自行车的。

sentences.en: You have to be certified to have a Dutch bike.
sentences.zh: 你得有执照才能拥有一辆荷兰自行车。

sentences.en: We also talked to someone that said they do have, at the Breda Station, bikes that you can get, but you need, like, a little ID card or, like, you know, payment card.
sentences.zh: 我们也跟一个人聊过，他说他们在布雷达车站确实有可以租的自行车，但你需要一张小身份证或者，你知道的，支付卡。

sentences.en: You can't just, like, do it with your cell phone and an app.
sentences.zh: 你不能直接用手机和一个应用程序来搞定。

sentences.en: But, anyways, we love the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，我们爱荷兰。

sentences.en: And I actually like Breda a little bit more than Amsterdam because you're not going to get killed here by a cyclist or a cohort of cyclists.
sentences.zh: 其实我比阿姆斯特丹更喜欢布雷达，因为在这里你不会被骑自行车的人或骑行大军给撞死。

sentences.en: We shouldn't have chose the bus.
sentences.zh: 我们本不该选公交车的。

sentences.en: We got to go to the bus.

sentences.zh: 我们为什么要在录这个？

sentences.en: That's when Bryce said he was the scan man, and Mark Harris came to mind because he has all the scan papers.
sentences.zh: 就是那时布莱斯说他是扫描侠，马克·哈里斯就浮现在脑海里，因为他有所有关于扫描的论文。

sentences.en: Bryce was just saying, and I don't know why the mic's just been by my side, is that he, or actually, do we want to dox him?
sentences.zh: 布莱斯刚才在说——我不知道为什么话筒一直搁在我旁边——他说，或者说，我们想不想曝光他？

sentences.en: We'll just say he lives in the hills of Australia.
sentences.zh: 我们就说他住在澳大利亚的山里吧。

sentences.en: But Mark has told some crazy, because Mark was a PIC, which is a pilot in command, person in charge.
sentences.zh: 但马克讲过一些疯狂的事情，因为马克曾是个 PIC，也就是机长，负责人。

sentences.en: I don't know what the actual acronym, pilot in command.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这个缩写具体是什么，飞行指挥官（Pilot in Command）。

sentences.en: And while both myself and Jake and a bunch of folks worked for Rapids, that's where I spent the firSt.
sentences.zh: 当我和杰克以及一大群人在 Rapids 工作时，那是我度过第一……

sentences.en: Can you explain what PIC is?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下什么是 PIC 吗？

sentences.en: It's just the person that is like an IC, but is a mentor at the same...
sentences.zh: 它就像是一个 IC（独立贡献者），但同时也是导师……

sentences.en: What I was going to say is, I only see one other person.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，我只看到另一个人。

sentences.en: I'm going to trust the person with the CPG under the C-shirt.
sentences.zh: 我要相信那个穿着 CPG under the C 恤的人。

sentences.en: I think Mark was the PIC of Rapids memory manager, RMM, but I don't actually fully know.
sentences.zh: 我想马克是 Rapids 内存管理器（RMM）的 PIC，但我其实不是很确定。
我听到好几个说是，所以……

sentences.en: Anytime you ask somebody at NVIDIA who the PIC is, and they say that it's more than one person, that means they haven't been at NVIDIA a very long time.
sentences.zh: 每当你问英伟达的某个人谁是 PIC，而他们说不止一个人时，那就意味着他们在英伟达待的时间还不够长。

sentences.en: It's just supposed to be one PIC for any given thing.
sentences.zh: 任何特定的事情本来就应该只有一个 PIC。

sentences.en: I mean, we should have Mark on, one, to talk about scans, but then he can tell this story himself.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们应该请马克来，一是聊聊扫描，然后他可以自己讲这个故事。

sentences.en: Say what you just said and nothing more.
sentences.zh: 把你刚才说的话再说一遍，别的什么都别加。

sentences.en: So, every listener, I guarantee you, is thinking that Python refers to the programming language.
sentences.zh: 所以，我敢保证，每个听众都会觉得 Python 指的是编程语言。

sentences.en: It refers to homing pythons that apparently can get up to several meters in length.
sentences.zh: 它指的是归巢蟒蛇，据说这种蟒蛇能长到好几米长。

sentences.en: And Mark tells this story, I'm sure he's told it to you, he's told it to me, where every once in a while, because he lives in the hills of Australia, these pythons show up in
sentences.zh: 马克讲过这样一个故事，我敢说他肯定也给你讲过，他跟我讲过，因为他住在澳大利亚的山里，这些蟒蛇会出现在

sentences.en: his backyard, and he has to...
I don't know how, but he collects the Python somehow, throws it in the back of what I assume is a truck, because that would be the right vehicle for a Python, and then he'll drive
sentences.zh: 我不知道他是怎么做到的，但他会把蟒蛇抓起来，扔到我猜是一辆卡车的后斗里，因为运蟒蛇就得用这种车，然后他会

sentences.en: it, like, literally hundreds, maybe not hundreds, but a hundred...
sentences.zh: 开车把它拉走，字面意思上的几百公里，也许不是几百，但也有个一百……

sentences.en: So, the story that he told me was, like, the first time he took it, and he drove it, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，他跟我讲的故事是，第一次他把它带走，开了大约

sentences.en: 40 kilometers, and he dropped it off, and then the sucker came back.
sentences.zh: 40公里，把它放生了，结果这货又自己找回来了。

sentences.en: And so, the next time, he researched how far they can home, and, like, the internet said, like, if you take it, like, 60 kilometers, it should be good.
sentences.zh: 于是第二次，他查了查它们能飞得多远，呃，网上说，如果你把它带到大概

sentences.en: And then, apparently, it kept coming back.

sentences.zh: 结果倒好，它居然又跑回来了。

sentences.en: At some point, the pythons just becomes your pet, you know?
If it's coming back that long, it's just your...
sentences.zh: 到头来，蟒蛇直接成你的宠物了，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't know how he knew that it was the same python, but I just assume that when you've lived in Australia long enough, you can tell the pythons apart.
sentences.zh: 既然它能跑那么远回来，那它就是你的……

sentences.en: And this, folks, is why I will be going to Australia for the first time this year, and
sentences.zh: 我不知道他是怎么看出这就是同一条蟒蛇的，但我想只要你在澳大利亚住得够久，你就能分辨出不同的蟒蛇。

sentences.en: I'm a little bit scared, because they have, like, all the deadliest spiders, like...
sentences.zh: 各位，这就是为什么我今年要第一次去澳大利亚，而且

sentences.en: Well, and you even know about the drop bears?
sentences.zh: 我有点害怕，因为那里有所有最致命的蜘蛛，比如……
对了，你听说过 drop bears（落地熊）吗？

sentences.en: Those are a reference to koala bears.
And I will say, they're actually pretty evil as well.
They're very cute, but if you actually just Google, or actually, link in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 不过我要说的是，它们其实也挺邪门的。
它们非常可爱，但如果你去谷歌一下，或者，节目简介里有链接。

sentences.en: Link in the show notes to a video of a koala bear on the ground going...
They make the most awful sound when they're crying for their parents.
sentences.zh: 节目简介里有视频链接，是一只趴在地上的考拉，在发出……

sentences.en: So cute in some circumstances, and they're actually mostly high a lot of the time, because they just live off of eucalyptus, which is some kind of carcinogen, or I don't know.
sentences.zh: 它们在呼唤父母时发出的声音太可怕了。

sentences.en: Anyways, I mean, we have Sean here.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下挺可爱的，而且它们其实大部分时间都处于高度兴奋状态，因为它们只靠吃桉树叶维生，那是一种致癌物，或者我也不清楚。

sentences.en: Should we rotate back to interviewing Sean?
sentences.zh: 总之，我是说，肖恩在这儿。
我们是不是该把话题转回采访肖恩了？

sentences.en: So, we tried to interview Sean earlier, but he was being...

sentences.zh: 所以，我们刚才试图采访肖恩，但他当时在……

sentences.en: Link in the show notes to a definition of that word, if you don't know what it means.

sentences.zh: 节目简介里有这个词的释义链接，如果你不知道它是什么意思的话。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll give it the Scrabble Dictionary.
sentences.zh: 韦氏词典、牛津词典，或者别的什么。
也许我们会给出《拼字游戏》词典的链接。

sentences.en: I think people need to up their vocabulary if they don't know the word.
How many points do you get for is absconded a good Scrabble word?
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果有人连这个词都不知道，他们得提升一下词汇量了。

sentences.en: Do you get a lot of points for that?
sentences.zh: 用“is absconded”在《拼字游戏》里能得多少分？这个词算是个好词吗？

sentences.en: It's not a great Scrabble word, but abscond, I believe, is seven letters.
If my math is wrong, then it's eight.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个很好的《拼字游戏》词汇，但“abscond”这个词，我记得是七个字母。
如果我算错了，那就是八个。

sentences.en: So, even though the highest scoring letter in that is going to be the C or the B, you're going to get an extra 50 points if you can spell that.
